Kattegat, the Sound and the Belts are inside. Meets the North Sea ECA at the same 57°44.8'N line, so passage North Sea <-> Baltic stays within ECA.

title: Canadian Arctic ECA
effNote: IN FORCE 1 Mar 2026 (NOx Tier III applies now); FUEL SULPHUR 0.10% NOT REQUIRED UNTIL 1 Mar 2027. Adopted 4 Oct 2024 by MEPC.392(82); entered into force 1 Mar 2026. SOx/PM (0.10% m/m) takes effect 1 Mar 2027 (12-month exemption of reg 14.7; Circ.778/Rev.5). NOx Tier III applies from entry into force (1 Mar 2026) to ships constructed on or after 1 Jan 2025 operating in the area (reg 13.5.1.3.1).
quote: The Canadian Arctic area comprises two segments: .1 starting at the Yukon mainland at 68°54'.00 N, 137°0'.00 W; following the coordinates listed below and ending at the north coast of Hans Island at 80°49'.91 N, 66°27'.40 W, connected by geodesic lines connecting the following coordinates in World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS84) datum: [points 1-50] .2 continuing from the south coast of Hans Island at 80°49'.29 N, 66°27'.04 W, following the coordinates listed below, and ending at the coast of Newfoundland and Labrador at 60°0'.00 N, 64°9'.60 W, connected by geodesic lines connecting the following coordinates in World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS84) datum: [points 51-179]
notes: WGS84, geodesic lines. Two open segments closed by the coast: 1-50 from the Yukon coast at 137°00'W, out to 86°N and round to the north coast of Hans Island, and 51-179 from the south coast of Hans Island south through Nares Strait, Baffin Bay and Davis Strait to the Labrador coast at 60°N. The ECA is the Canadian waters landward of these lines (the source gives no further description; which inland seas are included follows from the coast closing the lines). Point 179 (60°00'.00 N 64°09'.60 W) equals North American ECA Atlantic point 1 (60°00'00" 64°09'36"); point 178 is printed 56°43'.02 W while North American Atlantic point 2 is 56°43'00" W (0.02' difference, as printed in the two sources). Point 120 is printed '59°4'.46 W' (single-digit minutes), normalised to 059 04.46W. Coordinates are in degrees and decimal minutes (two decimals).

title: Mediterranean Sea ECA (SOx and PM)
effNote: Adopted 16 Dec 2022 by MEPC.361(79); entered into force 1 May 2024; ships exempt from reg 14.4 and 14.6 until 1 May 2025 (op. para 4), so 0.10% m/m applies from 1 May 2025. SOx/PM only: NOT a NOx Tier III ECA.
quote: In respect of the application of regulation 14.4, the Mediterranean Sea Emission Control Area for Sulphur Oxides and Particulate Matter includes all waters bounded by the coasts of Europe, Africa and Asia, and is described by the following coordinates: .1 the western entrance to the Straits of Gibraltar, defined as a line joining the extremities of Cape Trafalgar, Spain (36°11'.00 N, 6°02'.00 W) and Cape Spartel, Morocco (35°48'.00 N, 5°55'.00 W); .2 the Strait of Canakkale, defined as a line joining Mehmetcik Burnu (40°03'N, 26°11'E) and Kumkale Burnu (40°01'.00 N, 26°12'.00 E); and .3 the northern entrance to the Suez Canal excluding the area enclosed by geodesic lines connecting points 1-4 with the following coordinates: 1 31˚29'.00 N 32°16'.00 E; 2 31˚29'.00 N 32°28'.48 E; 3 31˚14'.00 N 32°32'.62 E; 4 31˚14'.00 N 32°16'.00 E
notes: DIFFERS from the Annex I Mediterranean special area: Annex I uses the meridian 005°36'W at Gibraltar and the parallel 41°N at the Black Sea entrance; the ECA uses the Trafalgar-Spartel line (further west) and the Canakkale (Dardanelles) line, so the Sea of Marmara and the Bosporus are OUTSIDE the ECA. The Suez Canal northern entrance area enclosed by points S1-S4 (Port Said approaches, geodesic lines) is EXCLUDED from the ECA. Mehmetcik Burnu is printed without decimal minutes (40°03'N, 26°11'E). The Gibraltar and Canakkale limits are straight lines between the named capes (geometry type not stated; 'line joining').

effNote: Adopted 26 Mar 2010 by MEPC.190(60); entered into force 1 Aug 2011; ECA SOx/PM requirements took effect 1 Aug 2012 (12-month exemption of reg 14.7). Fuel sulphur limit 1.00% m/m from 1 Aug 2012, 0.10% m/m from 1 Jan 2015 (reg 14.4.3). NOx Tier III for ships constructed on or after 1 Jan 2016 (Circ.778/Rev.5 note 6).
quote: the sea areas located off the Atlantic coasts of the United States, Canada, and France (Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon) and the Gulf of Mexico coast of the United States enclosed by geodesic lines connecting the following coordinates: POINT 1 60° 00' 00" N. 64° 09' 36" W. ... 206 25° 57' 24" N. 97° 08' 47" W.

Point 1 is on the Labrador coast at 60°N; point 206 is on the coast at the US/Mexico border (Rio Grande); the area is closed by the coastline, so the official boundary is the open line 1-206. Points 65-187 follow the Florida Straits / Cuba-Bahamas maritime boundary closely, so the ECA limit there is much less than 200 nm off Florida. Since MEPC.392(82) (in force 1 Mar 2026) the Canadian Arctic ECA adjoins this ECA at point 1 (60°00'N 064°09'36"W = Canadian Arctic point 179) and near point 2 (Canadian Arctic point 178 is printed as 60°00'.00 N 56°43'.02 W, i.e. 56°43'01.2"W, vs 56°43'00"W here). Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon (France) waters are inside.

effNote: IN FORCE 1 Mar 2026 (NOx Tier III applies now); FUEL SULPHUR 0.10% NOT REQUIRED UNTIL 1 Mar 2027. Adopted 4 Oct 2024 by MEPC.392(82); entered into force 1 Mar 2026. quote: 9.4 the Norwegian Sea is bounded by lines joining the following points: 69°47.6904' N; 030°49.059' E ... 62° N; 004°52.3464' E
notes: Source points are unnumbered; n = order as printed. Source precision varies (up to 4 decimals of minutes, e.g. 69°47.6904'); kept exactly, minutes only zero-padded (e.g. '031°6.2598'' -> '031 06.2598E', '74°2.9748'' -> '74 02.9748N'). '62° N' printed without minutes -> '62 00N'. 'Bounded by lines joining' (line type not stated). Open line closed by the Norwegian coast: starts at 69°47.69'N 030°49.06'E (near the Norway/Russia border), runs north-east to 73°23'N 036°29'E, then west along about 74°N to 73°15'N 014°09'E, then south-west and south to 62°N 004°52.35'E on the Norwegian coast. Northernmost point 74°29.80'N, so Svalbard (north of 76°N) is outside. At 62°N it adjoins the North Sea ECA (62°N east of 4°W). Annex VI cross-reference is by Annex II definition, so any future Annex II amendment would change it.

title: North Sea area
effNote: Designated by MEPC.36(28) (adopted 17 Oct 1989, in force 18 Feb 1991); special-area rules in effect 18 Feb 1991 (MEPC.37(28)).
quote: The North Sea area means the North Sea proper including seas therein with the boundary between: .1 the North Sea southwards of latitude 62° N and eastwards of longitude 4° W; .2 the Skagerrak, the southern limit of which is determined east of the Skaw by latitude 57° 44.8' N; and .3 the English Channel and its approaches eastwards of longitude 5° W and northwards of latitude 48° 30' N.
notes: Annex V only; NOT the same as Annex I 'North West European waters' (which extends west to 12°W and includes Irish Sea and Celtic Sea). Only the meridians/parallels are official (62°N, 4°W, 57°44.8'N, 5°W, 48°30'N); the two intersections 62°N/4°W and 48°30'N/5°W follow directly from the text. Coastal end points (1,3,4,6,7,8) were computed from Natural Earth 1:10m coastline and are NOT official. Interpretation: the regulation describes limits, not a point list; the encoding assumes the 4°W meridian runs from 62°N south to the Scottish coast, and the 5°W meridian runs from the Cornish coast south to 48°30'N, then 48°30'N east to Brittany. Confidence medium for the drawn geometry, high for the official values. The Skagerrak limit is the same 57°44.8'N line as the Baltic Sea area boundary. Status checked against MEPC.1/Circ.778/Rev.5 (9 May 2025; IMO circular, copy fetched from the Marshall Islands registry mirror, not imo.org).

title: North West European waters

quote: the North West European waters include the North Sea and its approaches, the Irish Sea and its approaches, the Celtic Sea, the English Channel and its approaches and part of the North East Atlantic immediately to the west of Ireland. The area is bounded by lines joining the following points: 48° 27' N on the French coast; 48° 27' N; 006° 25' W; 49° 52' N; 007° 44' W; 50° 30' N; 012° W; 56° 30' N; 012° W; 62° N; 003° W; 62° N on the Norwegian coast; 57° 44.8' N on the Danish and Swedish coasts
notes: Points 2-6 are official sea positions. Points 1, 7, 8a, 8b are given in the regulation only by latitude + coast; their longitudes are NOT official (computed from Natural Earth 1:10m coastline: Brittany mainland at 48°27'N, outermost Norwegian coast/island at 62°N, Skagen spit and Swedish coast at 57°44.8'N). The 48°27'N line from the French coast to 006°25'W passes across Ushant (Ile d'Ouessant). Point 8 closes the area across the Skagerrak: the Kattegat is outside NW European waters (it is in the Baltic Sea area). Source numbering in MEPC.75(40) was (i)-(viii); 8 split into 8a/8b here. Status checked against MEPC.1/Circ.778/Rev.5 (9 May 2025; IMO circular, copy fetched from the Marshall Islands registry mirror, not imo.org).

title: Wider Caribbean Region
effNote: Designated by MEPC.48(31) (adopted 4 Jul 1991, in force 4 Apr 1993); Annex V special-area discharge requirements in effect 1 May 2011 (MEPC.191(60), adopted 25 Mar 2010).
quote: The Wider Caribbean Region means the Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean Sea proper including the bays and seas therein and that portion of the Atlantic Ocean within the boundary constituted by the 30° N parallel from Florida eastward to 77°30' W meridian, thence a rhumb line to the intersection of 20° N parallel and 59° W meridian, thence a rhumb line to the intersection of 7°20' N parallel and 50° W meridian, thence a rhumb line drawn southwesterly to the eastern boundary of French Guiana.
notes: Points 2, 3, 4 are official. Point 1 longitude computed from Natural Earth coastline (not official). Point 5 is NOT given by coordinates in the regulation ('the eastern boundary of French Guiana', i.e. the French Guiana/Brazil border at the Oyapock river mouth); 04°20'N 051°40'W is an approximate drawing value only, low confidence. The rhumb line 4-5 runs south-westerly from 7°20'N 50°W. Includes the whole Gulf of Mexico (north of 30°N inside the Gulf too) and Caribbean Sea, the Bahamas and the Atlantic waters east of them inside the boundary. Annex V only (not an Annex I special area). Status checked against MEPC.1/Circ.778/Rev.5 (9 May 2025; IMO circular, copy fetched from the Marshall Islands registry mirror, not imo.org).
